items.fact: Season window: season/itinerary.cal say Jul-Sep, but best_season/seasonal_guidance/pro_tips say the route is best (and conditions degrade badly by high summer) in Late May-early July
items.prior_evidence: The one source that states a window (a club route page: July, August) backs neither side exactly, and aligning best_season would need month-by-month guidance and pro tips that no source gives, so nothing is changed. Club route page for Mount Buckner North Face: 'Seasons: July, August'. The summit route page and its comment give no months; a guide service offers the peak March-October.

items.fact: number/type of summit rappels
items.prior_evidence: Still no single count: the one club route page says only to rappel and downclimb the route, and the accounts that give a number disagree with each other and the row repeats all of them. The Mountaineers West Side page: 'Rappel and downclimb the climbing route' with no count or rope. Earlier first-hand accounts give one double-rope rap, two raps on 2x30 m, and three raps on a single 60 m; the row's rappels (1-2), descent_text (two, sometimes three) and climbing_route[3] (three) each carry one of these, so no single sourced value can be chosen without discarding another sourced one.

items.fact: one-way / round-trip approach distance
items.prior_evidence: The only new figure is a stated 14.0 mi round trip; no source states a one-way distance to the base or summit, and halving is not allowed. The Mountaineers West Side page gives Length 14.0 mi (round trip) and Nada Lake at 5.2 mi; earlier reports give 16-18 mi round trips. The row's one-way figures (approach ~8 mi, waypoint distMi 9.5-10, dist_km 12.9) and the 19-20 mi 3-day total have no stated one-way source.

items.fact: Total elevation gain/loss
items.prior_evidence: Sources disagree (8,000 ft from one report, 6,892 ft from the club route page) and the row's gain_ft already holds a sourced 8,000, but its itinerary days cannot be brought to that total without computing. The Mountaineers West Side page gives Elevation Gain 6,892 ft, split 5,600 ft trailhead-to-camp and 1,292 ft camp-to-summit; an earlier report gives 8,000 ft. Under the rule the row's sourced 8,000 is kept, but the itinerary days (5,300 + 1,700 + 200) and totalNote (~7,000) would need new computed day figures to agree with it, so nothing is patched.

items.fact: Whether a wilderness permit is needed
items.prior_evidence: Still split, and no source states the Wild Sky Wilderness permit rule outright either way. The forest's wilderness-regulations page names the free self-issue permit only for the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, and its Wild Sky page says only that wilderness regulations apply and some trailheads need a recreation pass; the peak page says only that passes are not required at either parking spot. None says a permit is or is not required in Wild Sky.

items.fact: Total route gain/distance vs. approach-to-camp leg only (dist_km 11.3)
items.prior_evidence: No source states a one-way trailhead-to-Austera distance; sources give only the trailhead-to-camp approach and the 2.8 mi camp-to-summit leg, which may not be added. Route database page: 2.8 mi one way from the Eldorado camp; encyclopedia page: about 3.5 mi from the dome SSE of Eldorado; the only whole-trip figures are multi-peak round trips.

items.fact: total elevation gain

items.fact: Thunder Basin high-camp elevation: 6,400 ft (waypoint) vs. ~5,180 ft (approach text and itinerary schedule)
items.prior_evidence: Each camp height is backed by its own single source (5,180 ft upper basin in one guide; 6,400 ft platforms in one first-hand report) and the row holds both, so the keep-what-the-row-holds rule cannot choose. Guide: upper Thunder Basin ~5,180 ft. First-hand report: 'Thunder Basin 6400' Camp' past the two small lakes at the top of the basin. A 2021 day-trip report (west ridge, different line) only notes terrain leveling out around 6,400 ft.

items.prior_evidence: No source states a round trip for the Southeast Route: the 26.8 mi figure includes the West Peak and the 25 mi / 7,300 ft day is a West Ridge ascent, so neither the 15.5 mi day sum nor the ~13 mi totalNote can be replaced. One report: 'Round Trip: 26.8 miles' for Tenpeak plus its West Peak. A 2021 report: '25 miles, 7,300ft' but by the west ridge. Wenatchee guide: 6 mi to Thunder Creek, no total.

items.fact: Total elevation gain

The Mystery Ridge enchainment report gives the Crowder day only; the peak's database page carries no route stats and its ascent list is not reachable (blocked, not archived). items.fact: total elevation gain: gain_ft 3,670 vs loss_ft 3,800 / itinerary 3,800 on an out-and-back

items.fact: Day-2 (summit push and exit) duration
items.prior_evidence: The one source gives day-2 legs (camp to summit 4-6 h, summit to trailhead 7-9 h) but no day-2 total, so days[1].hours and summitTimeHrs (10 h) cannot be set without adding legs. The club route page's trip profile lists camp to summit 4-6 h and summit to trailhead 7-9 h; the row's schedule (summit 9 AM from a 4 AM start, out by early evening) fits those legs, but the stated legs would have to be summed to replace the 10 h figure.

items.fact: Is the balanced summit block usually climbed? descent_text says most parties do not attempt it; beta/pro_tips/pro_needs say most parties protect/belay it
items.prior_evidence: No source states what most parties do with the summit block; each account describes only its own party (skipping it, rope-tossing it, or jugging it), so neither 'most do not attempt' nor 'most protect it' can be kept. Reports found describe single parties: one rope-tossed the block from the far side, one threw the rope over and jugged, others skipped it. None generalises.

items.fact: Car-to-car total time vs its own schedule
items.prior_evidence: One source's 11 h 15 min day supports totalHrs 11, but it started at 7:30 AM; making the 3:30 AM schedule end by 2:30-3 PM, or moving every row to that party's clock, would mean computing times the source does not state (the Katwalk and Bumblebee Pass times). A party left the car about 7:30 AM, reached the notch 4 h / 8.5 mi in, summited about 2 PM and called it roughly 11 h 15 min round trip. The row's schedule (3:30 AM start, back 5-6 PM) is 13.5-14.5 h.

items.fact: distance to camp: itinerary day 1 6.2 mi vs Cooney Lake waypoint at 8 mi
items.prior_evidence: No source states the one-way distance from the Foggy Dew trailhead to Cooney Lake on this line; the 8.5 mi figure is the whole length of Foggy Dew Trail #417, and a new day 1 would force a day 2 no source states. Two guides give round trips of 16.25 and 16 mi (the latter via Martin Creek); neither gives a one-way figure on the Foggy Dew line.

items.fact: Trailhead waypoint (4,700 ft) sits higher than the crag base (4,601 ft) although the approach hikes uphill to the crag
items.prior_evidence: No source states the parking elevation, so the 4,700 ft trailhead figure can be neither confirmed nor replaced; the club crag page gives a 4,600 ft high point with 200 ft of gain, which supports the crag's ~4,601 ft rather than the trailhead's 4,700 ft. Club crag page: high point 4,600 ft, elevation gain 200 ft, length 1.0 mi (but its intro also calls it a crag 'at 4,700 ft'); route database area page: 4,632 ft. None gives the lot's height, and deriving it from high point minus gain would be computed.

items.fact: round-trip distance and gain figures disagree
items.prior_evidence: Sources still disagree (7.0 mi / 3,500 ft on the hiking guide; 5.3 mi / 3,911 ft, 5.71 mi / 4,122 ft and others in reports), and none states the row's dist_km 5.6 or gain_ft 3,847, so there is no row value a source supports to keep. Hiking guide: 7.0 mi round trip, 3,500 ft, high point 6,129 ft; a report: 5.3 mi round trip, 3,911 ft to the true summit; a 2025 party: 5.71 mi, 4,122 ft; another: 3,556 ft. All round trips, none one-way, none matching the row.

items.fact: Total round-trip distance for the Standard Route
items.prior_evidence: No source states a Sentinel-only one-way or round-trip distance; found figures are per-day totals or the 32.6 mi Sentinel plus Old Guard outing. 2024 out-and-back party: per-day totals only; Sentinel + Old Guard: 32.6 mi round trip including road walk and a camp move.

items.fact: How long consolidated/climbable snow lasts on the route
items.prior_evidence: No source gives a snow window for the northwest ridge; the known accounts are a June 2020 big-snow ascent and a November 2025 thin-snow ascent. 2020 report met unusually large snowpack in June; 2025 report found thin snow over class 4 rock in November; neither states how long climbable snow lasts.

items.fact: Whole-outing gain/loss: gain_ft 6257 vs loss_ft 6157 on an out-and-back, with day 2 not counting the re-climb over Fourth Creek Pass
items.prior_evidence: The only stated car-to-car total (7,400 ft) cannot be adopted without computing new day figures for the itinerary, and loss_ft may not be written. Earlier sources give 7,400 ft for the trip and the approach legs (about 1,800 ft up to Fourth Creek Pass, ~1,200 ft down to Ingalls Creek); a single-day ascent gives only the net 4,853 ft rise. Setting gain_ft to 7,400 would contradict the itinerary days (2,000 + 4,257) unless their figures were recomputed, and loss_ft is out of bounds, so nothing is changed.

items.fact: road-walk and One Acre Lake distances from the current gate
items.prior_evidence: The one source for 2.25 mi measures the road walk from an older gate at the 2,100 ft switchback, not from the current gate at the bottom of Olney Creek Road where the row starts, so it does not support the row's 2.25 mi from the current gate. (3,700 ft)'. The row's gate is the road's start at about 1,700 ft, where a 2026 report gives about 5 miles of walking before leaving the road at ~3,700 ft. No source states the distance to One Acre Lake from the current gate. The row's 2.25 mi (approach, waypoint, schedule) and the bivy notes' five-to-six mile road walk therefore cannot be reconciled from a stated figure for the same gate.

items.fact: Climbing season window

Northeast Shoulder listing: a very good early-season climb (May-June). Peak route summary: the Kindy Ridge line uses the Snowking Glacier/snowfield in spring and early summer and the west ridge in late summer and fall. No source gives month-by-month conditions or an avalanche assessment for the early-season approach.
